newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 17.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:

* Top U.S. cigarette makers have begun talks that could lead to a settlement involving stricter goverment regulation, the formation of a large fund to cover the costs of smoking-related disease and advertising curbs.
* Ford reported better-than-expected first quarter profits, sending the stocks of the Big Three U.S. automakers higher.
* Compaq's earnings were ahead of analyst estimates but Apple Computer posted a larger-than-anticipated loss.
* BankAmerica and Fleet Financial posted higher earnings helped by cost-cutting and revenues from other businesses.
* March industrial production rose nine-tenths of one percent while housing starts held a good pace.
* Prosecutors in Germany have indicted CompuServe's head of on-line computer services on charges of alleged pornography trafficking.
* Time Warner reported sharply higher cash flow, ahead of forecasts. Results were helped by strong performances in nearly all divisions.
* The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 92.71 points at 6,679.87, extending its rally for a third day.
* AMR Corp, the parent of American Airlines, posted earnings that were mildly better-than-expected, although down.
* Harcourt General said it would make a $740 million cash offer for National Education, topping a friendly offer from Sylvan Learning Systems.
* Arkansas-based American Mineral Fields signed a multi-million dollar mining deal with Zaire's rebels.
* A U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission study has found investors are using state courts to bring fraud suits against companies.
* The eastern German economy remains troubled despite all the money western Germany has put into the region.
* The SEC defended its broad definition of insider trading in front of the U.S. Supreme Court.
* Hospitals and doctors complain that as health maintenance organizations become more like traditional insurers, they take longer to pay bills.
